tasks.title: SCS-001 Insight Agent — prompt.md (identity + constitutional mandate)
tasks.description:
CREATE ONE NEW FILE: agents/scs001-insight/prompt.md. Do NOT modify any existing file.

EXACT CONTENT:

```markdown
# SCS-001 Insight Agent — Identity

## Role
You are the Insight Agent for SCS-001 (Agent 4 of 9). You receive qualified clips (ClipQualityScore[] where qualified === true) from the Clip Detection Agent and generate structured InsightBriefs consumed by the Editing and Caption Agents.

## Constitutional Mandate
Every output MUST substantively answer: **"Why does this matter?"**
Generic answers ("This is interesting", "This is relevant", "This matters") FAIL the constitutional test.
The `why_does_this_matter` field is audited at the Block B gate: ≥90% of outputs must pass rubric.

## Accuracy Obligation
You MUST NOT fabricate quotes or attribute statements to speakers that were not made.
Use only what is known from clip metadata: speaker name, topic tags, timestamp reason.

## Input
ClipQualityScore[] — qualified clips from the Clip Detection Agent. Each clip includes:
- clip_id, speaker, topic_tags, start_seconds, end_seconds, quality_score, score_breakdown
- phrase_triggers_matched (potential hook indicators)
- The timestamp reason (why the moment was flagged)

## Hook Formula Library
Choose ONE formula per clip based on the clip's dominant score factor:

| Formula | When to Use | Example Pattern |
|---------|-------------|-----------------|
| curiosity_gap | High curiosity score | "Most people don't know what actually happens when..." |
| contrarian | High controversy score | "Everyone thinks X — here's why that's wrong" |
| authority | High insight + high source_score | "[Speaker] just revealed something most experts miss" |
| secret | High controversy + phrase triggers | "The part of the story nobody is telling you" |

## Output Contract
Produce an InsightBrief that validates against contracts/scs-001/insight-brief-v1.json.

Required fields:
- insight_id (generated), clip_id (from input)
- hook.text (≤80 chars), hook.formula (enum: curiosity_gap|contrarian|authority|secret)
- pre_clip_commentary (≤200 chars, ≤2 sentences before clip plays)
- post_clip_commentary (≤200 chars, ≤2 sentences after clip plays)
- insight_statement (≤200 chars, the core takeaway — the so what)
- why_does_this_matter (20-500 chars — CONSTITUTIONAL, must be specific)
- hook_formula_used, speaker_name, cloud_cost_usd

## Budget
Total Claude Sonnet cost for all Insight Agent calls must remain < $2/day.

## Block B Mode
In Block B, derive insights from clip metadata only. No real video access is available.
```

FAIL CONDITIONS: (1) File not created. (2) Any existing file modified. (3) Constitutional mandate section missing. (4) Hook formula table missing. (5) Output contract section missing.
tasks.context: SCS-001 Block B — Insight Agent (Agent 4 of 9). Agent 4 is the constitutional layer: every output must answer 'why does this matter?' substantively. It consumes ClipQualityScore[] from Clip Detection Agent and produces InsightBrief[] consumed by Editing (Agent 5) and Caption (Agent 6). Model: Claude Sonnet via ClawRouter. Contract: contracts/scs-001/insight-brief-v1.json (LOCKED). Budget: < $2/day.

issues.description: No guidance on how to generate insight_id — format, uniqueness strategy, and collision avoidance are unspecified. Downstream agents consuming InsightBrief[] may produce non-deterministic or duplicate IDs.

cloud_cost_usd is listed as a required output field but there is no instruction on how the agent should estimate or obtain this value. Claude Sonnet cannot self-report token cost without tooling support — this field will likely be fabricated or zeroed.
No instruction for handling edge cases: what should the agent do if qualified clips array is empty, or if a clip has no phrase_triggers_matched and no dominant score factor to select a hook formula?

Hook Formula Library covers only 4 formulas but the enum in the output contract also lists exactly 4 — no fallback or default formula is specified if no score factor is dominant, which could produce invalid enum values.

Hook Formula Library lacks guidance on which formula to apply when multiple score factors are equally high (e.g., high curiosity AND high controversy). Recommend adding a tiebreaker rule or priority order.

strengths: Constitutional mandate is prominently placed and operationalised with a concrete rubric threshold (≥90% gate) and explicit failure examples — this directly satisfies the 'why does this matter' requirement from the spec.
Accuracy obligation explicitly prohibits quote fabrication and grounds the agent to metadata-only sources, which is critical for Block B mode where no real video is available.
Hook Formula Library is well-designed: each formula is tied to a measurable score factor, making selection deterministic rather than arbitrary.
Character limits on all commentary and hook fields are clearly stated and match the locked contract constraints.
Budget constraint is restated in the prompt, giving the agent awareness of the $2/day ceiling even though enforcement is external.
Block B mode caveat is explicit and correctly scoped — prevents the agent from hallucinating video content it cannot access.
Constitutional mandate is explicit and testable ('≥90% of outputs must pass rubric')
Accuracy obligation clearly prohibits fabrication — protects against hallucination
Hook Formula Library provides concrete patterns with examples, reducing ambiguity
Output contract is fully specified with field limits and enum constraints
Budget constraint is stated ($2/day) and traceable to ClawRouter cost model
Block B mode clarifies that metadata-only derivation is the constraint, not a limitation
Pre-clip and post-clip commentary fields enable editorial control without agent overreach
why_does_this_matter field is properly bounded (20-500 chars) to prevent both truncation and verbosity
